title: Bank of Japan holds interest rate at 1.25%, accelerates ETF sales
summary:
The Bank of Japan kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25 per cent on October 30, in an 8–1 vote, with one board member favouring a hike to 1.5 per cent. 
The central bank also unanimously approved accelerating annual ETF sales from 330 billion yen to 860 billion yen, citing smooth disposals since January 2026 and expanding stock market trading volumes.

title: South India's cotton yarn prices steady amid weak demand, cash crunch
summary:
Indian cotton yarn prices stayed stable in Tiruppur and Mumbai as demand remained subdued and payment constraints worsened across the textile value chain.
Tiruppur steadied after a ₹3–5 (~$0.03–0.05) per kg fall earlier this week, while Mumbai faced tight liquidity and limited supply.
Gujarat cotton fell by ₹500 per candy as spinning mills awaited clarity on duty-free import extension.

title: US GDP grows 3.4% in Q3 as investment & spending rise
summary:
US real GDP grew at an annual rate of 3.4 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, up from 2.2 per cent in the second quarter, the BEA's advance estimate showed.
Investment, consumer spending and government spending lifted growth, partly offset by lower exports, while imports increased.
Private domestic demand rose 4.9 per cent; PCE inflation eased to 2.1 per cent.

title: China drives US Upland cotton sales growth as Pima sales plunge: USDA
summary:
US Upland cotton export sales rose 8 per cent to 216,500 RB in the week ended October 22, with China the top buyer at 52,100 RB and demand also from Turkiye, Vietnam and Indonesia.
Exports fell 18 per cent to 160,800 RB, led by shipments to Vietnam.
Pima cotton demand weakened sharply, with sales down 95 per cent and exports down 56 per cent.

title: Bangladesh customs crackdown tests $1.31 bn fabric imports
summary:
Chattogram Customs locked 467 import consignments in July–September 2026, up 29.4 per cent, with fines and revenue at 582 million taka.
TexPro puts selected fabric imports at $1.313 billion in July–August, down 2.75 per cent, as China’s share rose to 82.8 per cent.
Apparel exports grew 6.10 per cent, but rule shifts, bond checks and clearance delays are raising compliance and sourcing risks.

title: Drewry WCI falls 3.4% as US import demand weakens
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index fell 3.40 per cent to $4,429 per FEU in the week ending October 29, led by lower Transpacific rates as US import demand eased.
Shanghai-Los Angeles rates dropped 6 per cent; Drewry expects further declines next week.
Asia-Europe rates were stable to slightly higher, while weak demand, capacity management, Suez, Hormuz and US trade policy remain key influences.

title: India's $1 bn fabric exports face new customs rules on Nov 1
summary:
India will require exporters of specified cotton, synthetic and knitted fabrics to declare flame-retardant status in shipping bills from November 1.
TexPro values the corresponding fabric basket at $1.037 billion in FY 2025-26, with April-July 2026 exports up 3.79 per cent to $337.03 million.
PLI Round 4 opens the same day; Sri Lanka and Bangladesh made up about 42.3 per cent of exports.

title: US' Crocs raises FY26 outlook as HeyDude returns to growth
summary:
Crocs has lifted its FY26 revenue growth outlook to about 3 per cent and adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance to $14.45-$14.65 after robust Q3 execution. 
Third-quarter revenue rose 4.6 per cent to $1.04 billion and net income increased 48.7 per cent to $216.8 million.  
HeyDude revenue climbed 6.1 per cent, returning to growth, while Crocs Brand international sales rose 11.8 per cent.

title: Turkiye’s apparel exports fall 9.3%: Is Egypt gaining more ground now?
summary:
Turkiye’s apparel exports (HS 61-62) fell 9.3 per cent to $10.60 billion in January-August 2026 from the same 2024 period as pressure rose on producers.
Textile exports across HS 50-60 were nearly flat at $7.94 billion, while apparel imports rose 28.8 per cent to $2.92 billion.
Orta Anadolu is closing Kayseri production facilities and TYH Tekstil remains in court-supervised concordat.

title: US apparel import values fall 7%: Why are retail prices still rising?
summary:
US apparel CPI rose 3.4 per cent in the year to September 2026, outpacing a 1.3 per cent rise in apparel manufacturing import prices.
The gain was nearly five times the 0.7 per cent rise in core goods, while headline inflation reached 3.7 per cent.
Imports under HS 61 and 62 fell 7.0 per cent by value in January-August, and exporters must factor July Section 301 duties into landed costs.

title: US' Columbia raises FY26 sales outlook after stronger Q3
summary:
Columbia Sportswear has raised the low end of its FY26 sales and diluted earnings per share outlook after a stronger-than-expected third quarter, supported by earlier wholesale shipments, improving US DTC trends and international momentum. 
Q3 net sales rose 2 per cent to $962.6 million and net income increased to $84.7 million from $52 million. 
Operating margin reached 11.4 per cent.

title: Why garment construction matters for apparel brand margins
summary:
Apparel brands can manage manufacturing costs by simplifying garment construction, though savings are limited if fabric use is unchanged.
Belinda Jacobs of Techpacks.co says complex seams, linings, pockets, speciality stitching and custom fasteners add labour across production runs.
She warns cutting stitching quality, seam allowances or reinforcement can raise defects, returns and hurt trust.

title: EU takes 49% of Bangladesh RMG exports: What happens after EBA?
summary:
Bangladesh’s EU EBA garment preferences could continue to end-2029 after its scheduled LDC graduation on November 24, 2026, or to end-2032 if the UN approves an extension.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 grants a three-year transition, but rules of origin will shape future apparel eligibility.
The EU took $19.06 billion, or 49.25 per cent, of Bangladesh’s FY2025–26 RMG exports.

title: Japan’s apparel imports rise 3.1% in first half of FY27
summary:
Japan’s apparel imports rose 3.1 per cent to 2,034,156 million yen (~$12.88 billion) in April–September 2026.
Yarn and fabric imports grew 13.6 per cent, while exports rose 8.4 per cent.
Textile machinery exports climbed 17.2 per cent to 161,172 million yen.
In September, apparel imports rose 6.1 per cent and textile machinery exports grew 15.8 per cent.

title: AAFA files rebuttal to Europe's counterfeit watch list
summary:
The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the European Commission to strengthen action against online counterfeiting, naming Meta, Alibaba.com, AliExpress and DHGate as platforms of concern. 
AAFA cited safety failures in 16 of 39 counterfeit products tested and called for stronger seller verification, proactive detection and tougher action against repeat offenders.

title: NG Textiles secures WRAP certification for Villa Nueva facility
summary:
NG Textiles has secured WRAP certification for its Villa Nueva facility, valid from October 2026 to October 2027, strengthening its responsible manufacturing credentials.
Employing around 770 workers and producing 390,000 garments monthly, the company offers US brands integrated apparel production, duty-free access under CAFTA-DR and faster nearshore delivery.

title: Ethiopia's apparel exports shift towards US as Europe's share declines
summary:
Ethiopia's apparel exports are shifting towards North America, whose share rose to 61.38 per cent in January–September 2026 as Europe's fell to 35.03 per cent.
Overall exports slipped 3.37 per cent to $250 million, but shipments to North America rose 14.98 per cent to $153.46 million.
The US remained the top destination at $143.59 million, while European demand contracted.
